Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-615", "title": "Organ Donation", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Organ donation takes healthy organs and tissues from one person for transplantation into another."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Experts say that the organs from one donor can save or help as many as 50 people."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Organs you can donate include: Internal organs: Kidneys, heart, liver, pancreas, intestines, lungs Skin Bone and bone marrow Cornea Most organ and tissue donations occur after the donor has died."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "But some organs and tissues can be donated while the donor is alive."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "People of all ages and background can be organ donors."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "If you are under age 18, your parent or guardian must give you permission to become a donor."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "If you are 18 or older you can show you want to be a donor by signing a donor card."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "You should also let your family know your wishes."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Health Resources and Services Administration"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1437", "title": "Acute Lymphocytic Leukemia", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Leukemia is a term for cancers of the blood cells."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Leukemia starts in blood-forming tissues such as the bone marrow."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Your bone marrow makes the cells which will develop into white blood cells, red blood cells, and platelets."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Each type of cell has a different job: White blood cells help your body fight infection Red blood cells deliver oxygen from your lungs to your tissues and organs Platelets help form clots to stop bleeding When you have leukemia, your bone marrow makes large numbers of abnormal cells."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "This problem most often happens with white blood cells."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "These abnormal cells build up in your bone marrow and blood."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "They crowd out the healthy blood cells and make it hard for your cells and blood to do their work."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "What is acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL)?"}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Acute lymphocytic leukemia is a type of acute leukemia."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "It's also called ALL and acute lymphoblastic leukemia."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "\"Acute\" means that it usually gets worse quickly if it's not treated."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "ALL is the most common type of cancer in children ."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "In ALL, the bone marrow makes too many lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "These cells normally help your body fight infection."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "But in ALL, they are abnormal and cannot fight infection very well."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "They also crowd out the healthy cells, which can lead to infection, anemia , and easy bleeding."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "These abnormal cells can also spread to other parts of the body, including the brain and spinal cord."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "What causes acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL)?"}, {"id": "S018", "text": "ALL happens when there are changes in the genetic material (DNA) in bone marrow cells."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "The cause of these genetic changes is unknown."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "However, there are certain factors that raise your risk of ALL."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Who is at risk for acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL)?"}, {"id": "S022", "text": "The factors that raise your risk of ALL include: Being male Being white Being over age 70 Having had chemotherapy or radiation therapy Having been exposed to high levels of radiation Having certain genetic disorders , such as Down syndrome What are the symptoms of acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL)?"}, {"id": "S023", "text": "The signs and symptoms of ALL include: Weakness or feeling tired Fever or night sweats Easy bruising or bleeding Petechiae, which are tiny red dots under the skin."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Shortness of breath Weight loss or loss of appetite Pain in the bones or stomach Pain or feeling of fullness below the ribs Swollen lymph nodes - you may notice them as painless lumps in the neck, underarm, stomach, or groin Having had many infections How is acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL) diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Your health care provider may use many tools to diagnose ALL and figure out which subtype you have: A physical exam A medical history Blood tests, such as Complete blood count (CBC) with differential Blood chemistry tests such as a basic metabolic panel (BMP) , comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) , kidney function tests , liver function tests , and electrolyte panel Blood smear Bone marrow tests ."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "There are two main types - bone marrow aspiration and bone marrow biopsy."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Both tests involve removing a sample of bone marrow and bone."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "The samples are sent to a lab for testing."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Genetic tests to look for gene and chromosome changes If you are diagnosed with ALL, you may have additional tests to see whether the cancer has spread."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "These include imaging tests and a lumbar puncture , which is a procedure to collect and test cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "What are the treatments for acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL)?"}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Treatments for ALL include: Chemotherapy Radiation therapy Chemotherapy with stem cell transplant Targeted therapy, which uses drugs or other substances that attack specific cancer cells with less harm to normal cells Treatment is usually done in two phases: The goal of the first phase is to kill the leukemia cells in the blood and bone marrow."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "This treatment puts the leukemia into remission."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Remission means that the signs and symptoms of cancer are reduced or have disappeared."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "The second phase is known as post-remission therapy."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Its goal is to prevent a relapse (return) of the cancer."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "It involves killing any remaining leukemia cells that may not be active but could begin to regrow."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Treatment during both phases also usually includes central nervous system (CNS) prophylaxis therapy."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "This therapy helps prevent the spread of leukemia cells to the brain and spinal cord."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "It may be high dose chemotherapy or chemotherapy injected into the spinal cord."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "It also sometimes includes radiation therapy."}]}, {"id": "MLP-5321", "title": "Women's Health Checkup", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Regular checkups with your health care provider are different from appointments for sickness or injury."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Your checkups, which are also called well-woman exams, include physical exams as well as preventive care."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "They can help find health problems early, when they may be easier to treat."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Your checkup is usually done by a provider with special training in caring for women."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It will include screenings for chronic diseases."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "As a woman, you may also get special exams and screenings, such as: A pelvic exam to check the health of your reproductive organs."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Your provider will look at your vulva, vagina, and cervix."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "They will also do an internal exam to feel the size and shape of your internal organs such as the uterus and ovaries."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "A cervical cancer screening , which uses a Pap test , an HPV test , or both."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "The tests can help prevent cervical cancer ."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "A Pap test checks for cervical cancer and for abnormal cells that could turn into cancer."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "An HPV test looks for the types of HPV which can cause cervical cancer."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "For both tests, your provider will take a sample of cells from the surface of your cervix and send them to a lab to be examined under a microscope."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "A clinical breast exam to check for breast cancer ."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Your provider will feel and look at your breasts and armpit area for lumps or other changes."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "They may also recommend a mammogram , which is an x-ray picture of your breast."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Which tests you get and how often you need them will depend on your age, overall health, and family health history ."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "In some cases, your provider may also recommend other tests as well."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "For example, if you have a family history of certain cancers, your provider may recommend genetic testing ."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "During your checkup, you and your provider may also talk about other issues, such as: Birth control or family planning Menopause Menstrual concerns Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) Vaccines Your overall physical health and mental well-being , including suggestions on how to have a healthy lifestyle To make the most of your next checkup, bring a list of any questions or concerns you have, so you can talk about them with your provider."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1706", "title": "Prescription Drug Misuse", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "If you take a medicine in a different way than your health care provider prescribed, it's called prescription drug misuse."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It could be: Taking medicine prescribed for someone else."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Taking a larger dose than you are supposed to."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Taking the medicine in a different way than you are supposed to."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "For example, instead of swallowing your tablets, you might crush them and then snort or inject them."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Using the medicine for another purpose, such as getting high."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Misusing some prescription drugs can lead to addiction ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "These include opioids , sedatives, tranquilizers, and stimulants."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Drug addiction is a chronic brain disease."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "It causes a person to take drugs repeatedly despite the harm they cause."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Who is at risk for prescription drug misuse?"}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Prescription drug misuse can affect anyone at any age, including teenagers and older adults."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "It can happen if you need certain medicines to treat a medical condition, reduce pain after an injury or surgery, or for chronic pain ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Risk factors can include: A lack of knowledge about the prescription drug and possible risks A previous addiction to other substances, including alcohol and tobacco Certain mental health conditions What are the risks of prescription drug misuse?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Prescription drug misuse can have serious medical consequences."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Every medicine has some risk of side effects, which providers think about when prescribing medicines."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "People who misuse these drugs may not know the risks."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Some medicines may not be safe for them, especially at higher doses or when taken with other medicines."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "What are treatments for prescription drug misuse?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Treatment for prescription drug misuse often includes medicines and counseling, but it depends on the type of drug and your needs."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "The counseling may be individual, family, and/or group therapy."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "It can help you: Understand why prescription drug misuse began Learn how to change unhealthy patterns of thinking and behavior Manage personal problems and develop positive relationships Learn how to manage cravings and avoid situations that could lead to a relapse Stopping or cutting back on prescription drugs used for a while, may cause different symptoms for different drugs."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Your provider will work with you to manage the symptoms as your body gets used to being taken off the medicine."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "How can I prevent problems with taking prescription drugs?"}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Providers and pharmacists play a role in preventing or reducing prescription drug misuse, but you can also take steps to reduce your risk."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "A few ways to help reduce your risk and make sure that you are using any prescription medicines correctly include: Talk to your provider about any other prescription medicines, over-the-counter-medicines , and supplements that you're taking to see if it is safe to take the prescription drug with them."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Follow the directions carefully and take medicine as prescribed."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "If you're taking prescription drugs for pain and it isn't working, don't stop or change the amount you're taking without talking to your provider."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "If your provider prescribes opioids, ask about the risks and benefits of taking the medicine, and if another medicine with less risk of addiction could be used."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1245", "title": "Thymus Cancer", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "The thymus is a small organ in your upper chest, under your breastbone."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Before birth and during childhood, the thymus helps the body make a type of white blood cell."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "These cells help protect you from infections."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "You are more likely to get it if you have other diseases such as myasthenia gravis, lupus or rheumatoid arthritis."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Other times, thymus cancer can cause: A cough that doesn't go away Chest pain Trouble breathing Doctors use a physical exam, imaging tests, and a biopsy to diagnose thymus cancer."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "The most common treatment is surgery to remove the tumor."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Other options include radiation therapy, chemotherapy, and hormone therapy."}]}]
